spec.description: Tells apart a frozen server from a network-side failure, and shows what the server looked like before it went down.

options.content:
**Timeline rows run from most basic (top) to most dependent (bottom).** Find the *first* row that turns red to see what went down first.

- **Top row red together with everything below** → the whole machine stopped (freeze, kernel hang, power). Nothing was recorded while it was down.
- **Top row green, but link / router / internet rows red** → the machine was alive and the *network side* failed (NIC, cable, switch, router, ISP). If the localhost rows (AdGuard, SSH, Nextcloud, Minecraft) stayed green, the services themselves were fine.
- The panels below show what the server looked like *before* it went down (temperature, memory/IO stalls, NIC errors, link flaps).

spec.title: What went down, and in what order?
spec.description: UP/DOWN per check. A frozen server shows DOWN on every row, because nothing was recorded. Network-only failures leave the top rows green.

spec.title: Uptime
spec.description: Time since the last boot. A short uptime after you restarted is expected; a short uptime you did NOT cause means it rebooted by itself.

spec.title: Uptime (a drop = reboot, a gap = server stopped recording)
spec.description: Sawtooth. Every drop to zero is a boot. A gap before the drop is the time the server was frozen and recording nothing.

spec.title: Pressure stalls (time tasks waited)
spec.description: Share of time processes were stalled waiting on memory / disk / CPU. A climb right before an outage points at memory thrashing or a struggling disk.

spec.title: OOM kills
spec.description: Any bar here means the kernel ran out of memory and killed a process.

spec.title: Link flaps (carrier changes)
spec.description: Each bar is the NIC link going up or down. Repeated flaps point at the cable, switch port, or NIC/driver.

spec.title: Link speed
spec.description: Negotiated speed. A drop from 1 Gbit to 100/10 Mbit usually means a bad cable or port.

spec.title: Kernel limits in use (conntrack, file descriptors)
spec.description: A full conntrack table makes new connections fail while the machine looks healthy.

spec.title: Probe latency
spec.description: Rising latency or timeouts to the router before a drop means the local network was degrading first.

spec.title: Host health (what the server looked like before it went down)
